eligible.content: I'll give that a try. I've got some compost in the shed, so I'll spread a bit around the base of the plants tomorrow. I'm hoping it helps them hold on until the rain comes.
That sounds like a perfect plan! Hopefully, that extra organic matter will help them through the dry spells. Keep us posted on how it goes!

sources.content: I'm glad we agree on the first step. I'm especially worried about the ones in smaller pots—they seem to dry out faster. Have you ever tried using pebbles or something to help retain moisture?

Yes, using things like pebbles or mulch can definitely help! They can help regulate the temperature and retain moisture around the roots, which is especially useful for those smaller pots that dry out quickly. Have you tried using some sort of mulch, or maybe a layer of rocks, around the pots to see how that helps?
That's exactly what I was thinking. I've started putting a few pebbles around the base of the plants, and it seems to be making a difference. Do you think adding a bit of compost might help too?

That sounds like a great idea! Adding some compost to the soil around your plants should definitely help. Compost adds organic matter that retains moisture and adds nutrients, so it should help those plants feel a bit more comfortable in the heat!
I'll give that a try. I've got some compost in the shed, so I'll spread a bit around the base of the plants tomorrow. I'm hoping it helps them hold on until the rain comes.
That sounds like a perfect plan! Hopefully, that extra organic matter will help them through the dry spells. Keep us posted on how it goes!
